title: You’ve read it.
paragraphs:
You’ve read it.
You’ve paused at it.
And something in you knows… this isn’t just a random line in Scripture.
“The Nephilim were on the earth in those days…” — Genesis 6:4
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

This passage isn’t just about mysterious beings.
It’s about how far humanity had fallen—and why judgment was coming.
The Scene Before the Flood

The world in Genesis 6 is not neutral.
It’s not morally confused.
It is corrupted to the core.
“The Lord saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every intention of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” (Genesis 6:5)
Read that again.
Only evil. Continually.

God saw it.
You would have seen it too.
So Who Were the Nephilim?
There are three main interpretations—but only one thing is certain:
1. Fallen Angel View (Most Dramatic)

“Sons of God” = fallen angels
“Daughters of men” = human women
This view suggests a supernatural rebellion, producing the Nephilim—described as:
“mighty men… men of renown” (Genesis 6:4)
Cross-reference tension appears in:

Jude 1:6 — angels who left their proper domain
2 Peter 2:4 — angels cast into chains of darkness
This interpretation sees the Nephilim as hybrid giants, symbols of extreme corruption.
2. Sethite View (Moral Collapse)

“Sons of God” = descendants of Seth (godly line)
“Daughters of men” = descendants of Cain (rebellious line)
This isn’t about angels—it’s about compromise.
God’s people intermarried with rebellion, and holiness collapsed.
Result?
A generation of spiritual giants in reputation—but not in righteousness.
3. Tyrant Kings View (Power Corruption)

“Sons of God” = powerful rulers
They took women by force—building dominance, violence, and fame.
The Nephilim here represent men who became legends through oppression.
But Here’s the Real Point
You’re focusing on the Nephilim.
God was focused on the human heart.
“Every intention… only evil continually.”
That’s the diagnosis.

Not just them.
Us.
Spiritual Diagnosis
You don’t need to be a Nephilim to be condemned.
You just need a heart untouched by God.
“All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
You knew.
Why This Matters

Right after mentioning the Nephilim…
God announces judgment.
The flood wasn’t random.
It was response.
“I will blot out man whom I have created…” (Genesis 6:7)
That’s not just history.
That’s justice.
But Then—Grace Breaks In
One line changes everything:
“But Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord.” — Genesis 6:8
But.
Grace enters where judgment was deserved.
And that’s the Gospel.
The True and Better Rescue
The ark saved Noah from water.
Jesus Christ saves you from wrath.
“For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” — Romans 6:23

Not by works.
Not by lineage.
Not by avoiding being a “Nephilim.”
Only by grace through faith.
Decision Moment

You can study the Nephilim your whole life…
And still miss salvation.
This isn’t about ancient giants.
This is about your standing before a holy God.

Judgment is real.
Corruption is deep.
Grace is available.
But not forever.
Open Loop

Just like in Noah’s day…
There is still time before the door closes.
But not much.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
